decisions.statement: The change to answer is named by the first word.
A call naming no change is refused rather than reaching every change.
That refusal names every change a draft runs.
The arguments the change takes are read from standard input.
An argument is a line `key: value` or `key <fence>` opening a body `<fence>` alone closes.
The fence is the caller's to pick.
A body opened `key <fence> no-newline` keeps no newline on its last line.
The key `at` names a path, read against the repository root.
Two drafts leave two sets of edits in the order the runs were made.
The edits answered are kept beside the calling agent's page.
A draft lands nothing.
A draft names where the edits are kept and the call that lands them.
The key `message` is refused rather than carried into a commit that is not made.
The key `draft` is refused.
The key `measure` is refused.
A word naming an act over the edits kept is read here as a change to answer.
A draft is handed the world the edits kept before that draft leave.
A draft that refuses keeps nothing and says why the draft refused.
A draft whose writer owes reading is refused before that draft's edits are kept.
An agent whose page is nowhere is refused rather than answered with nothing.
No check runs over a draft.
No flag other than the help flag is said on the command line.
The help flag is answered with what a draft does and what a draft takes.
The help flag is read before the arguments are, so nothing need be piped in.
A draft's answer names every page written.
A draft that threw after keeping its edits names those edits in its refusal.
A draft that threw before keeping anything says nothing of what it kept.
A draft names each thing it did in the order it did them.
No redirect carries that answer to a file.
A draft is ended at the ceiling on the wall clock its page states.
A draft ended that way keeps nothing and says nothing.
A change past the processor seconds its page allows keeps nothing.

definition: the command answering one change and keeping its edits rather than landing them
